title: Sonata No. 1, Op. 96
identity: Edvard Moritz’s *Sonata No. 1, Op. 96* is a 1938 work for E-flat alto saxophone and piano published by Southern Music and dedicated to Cecil Leeson. Historic discography and reviews document Leeson’s recording with pianist Josef Wagner; a contemporaneous review characterized it as melodic and not written to exploit the saxophone’s spectacular effects.

evidence.claim: Southern Music identifies Op. 96 for alto saxophone and piano, four movements, a 27-minute duration, and an advancing-player descriptor.
Music history event page identifies the 1939 sonata for E-flat alto saxophone and piano among works written for Cecil Leeson.
Contemporary review identifies Decca album 187 and a Leeson-Wagner performance, and describes the work as melodic while noting it does not exploit the saxophone spectacularly.
Purdue digital collection result lists the 1938 work in a saxophone sonata discography and cites a recording of Leeson.

review_focus: The period review’s melodic description and stated avoidance of spectacular effects are useful interpretive context; verify the solo writing in the score before drawing technical conclusions.
